ncei:5256559.title: Chambers, Nebraska
ncei:5256559.narrative: The tornado touched down 3 miles south of Chambers and preceeded slowly southeast. No damage was reported as the tornado tracked to near Highway 281, 6 miles southeast of Chambers, before lifting.

ncei:5261388.title: Eureka, South Dakota
ncei:5261388.narrative: A tornado touched down north of Eureka.  The tornado remained in open country and caused no damage. Path length and width were estimated.

ncei:5272110.title: Sylacauga, Alabama
ncei:5272110.narrative: The F2 tornado began at 3:42 pm near the intersection of Forest Glen Rd. and Odens Mill Rd.,   in the Oak Grove Community.  It traveled northeast crossing US 280 and ended at 3:45 pm near Shirtee Creek in the Odena Community.  The Red Cross and the local Emergency Management Agency estimate that 15 people were injured,  two critically.  Forty to 50 homes were damaged with 7 of the homes sustaining significant damage.  Ten mobile homes were totally destroyed.  Several outbuildings and sheds were destroyed and numerous trees were blown down or uprooted along the entire path.  The tornado path was 3.1 miles long and 400 yards wide at its widest point.  Beg:  33 10.930/86 18.818  End:  33 12.502/86 16.176

ncei:5136038.title: Del Rio, Texas
ncei:5136038.narrative: A small tornado was produced by a supercell storm that had formed in Mexico and moved northeastward into the U.S.  The tornado destroyed a small barn, overturned trailers and killed several cattle. The report was made simultaneously by a rancher and a park ranger.

ncei:5136530.title: Port St Joe, Florida
ncei:5136530.narrative: A waterspout developed over St Joseph Bay and moved onshore.  An office building sustained minor damage.  Reported by the Gulf County EMA.

ncei:5145701.title: Newcastle, Texas
ncei:5145701.narrative: A brief tornado was reported. No damage or injury reports were received.

ncei:5147617.title: Eakly, Oklahoma
ncei:5147617.narrative: This tornado formed in Washita County and dissipated on the Washita/Caddo Couny line.

ncei:5681816.title: Vaiden, Mississippi
ncei:5681816.narrative: Mississippi Highway Partrol sighted the brief touchdown of this tornado.

ncei:5681966.title: Aloha, Louisiana
ncei:5681966.narrative: Tornado occurred over an unpopulated wooded area.

ncei:5705188.title: Cement, Oklahoma
ncei:5705188.narrative: Tornado A6 (Caddo County portion). See summary at end of May 3rd storm reports.

ncei:5710984.title: Harlowton, Montana
ncei:5710984.narrative: A driver on U.S. Highway 191 and an amateur radio operator reported a thin rope like tornado that was on the ground over rural areas for around 15 minutes.

ncei:5714993.title: Palmetto, Florida
ncei:5714993.narrative: A tornado briefly touched down without damage along the 1500 block of U.S. Highway 301 in Palmetto.

ncei:5629745.title: Wilmington, North Carolina
ncei:5629745.narrative: A GUSTNADO INDUCED BY MICROBURST, TOSSED A STATION WAGON 100FT, TIPPED A TRUCK ON IT'S SIDE A DAMAGED A CONVENIENCE STORE AND A MANUFACTURING PLANT ON 23RD STREET.

ncei:5634207.title: Islamorada, Florida
ncei:5634207.narrative: Tornado moved from the south across Islamorada near  MM 80. Extensive damage to homes and businesses. Widespread tree and vegetation loss.

ncei:5637197.title: Moody, Alabama
ncei:5637197.narrative: The tornado began 2.3 miles north-northeast of Moody and just west of US 411.  The tornado crossed US 411 where a large church and associated buildings, some recently constructed were destroyed.  The tornado traveled on an east-northeast track moving through relatively rural areas.  It affected a portion of CR 174 and then crossed US 231 just south of Wattsville.  The tornado damaged a number of buildings in the Coal City area including a mobile home where two people were killed and three children were injured.  The tornado ended in an open area just east of Coal City.  Emergency Management for St. Clair County reported that 26 homes were destroyed, 30 homes suffered major damage, and 59 sustained minor damage.  This included 42 mobile homes.

ncei:5641466.title: Hindsboro, Illinois
ncei:5641466.narrative: A tornado briefly touched down destroying a machine shed 2 miles north of Hindsboro.  No injuries were reported and no damage estimate was available.

ncei:5602095.title: Mc Bee, South Carolina
ncei:5602095.narrative: The F1 tornado that crossed over from Kershaw county diminished to an F0 tornado and only took down some trees.

ncei:5611799.title: Pine Spgs, Texas
ncei:5611799.narrative: A tornado was reported by a rancher near the Hudspeth County line 10 miles south of U.S. Highway 62/180 in the Sierra Diablo Mountains.

ncei:5612777.title: Andrews, Texas
ncei:5612777.narrative: Tornado formed about 4.5 miles west of the intersection of U.S. Highway 385 and FM 1967. Reported by SKYWARN spotter.  This storm entered from Gaines County and became a supercell.  The storm was moving to the right of the upper flow, partly due to its dependence on the front for a low-level focus.

ncei:5617671.title: Douglas, Georgia
ncei:5617671.narrative: Large trees and power lines were blown down.

ncei:10338432.title: Ncz090, North Carolina
ncei:10338432.narrative: A tornado touched down near Faison on Route 403 destroying two trailers and ripping the roof off of a house.

ncei:10349714.title: North Knoxville, Tennessee
ncei:10349714.narrative: An large awning was blown off of a house.  Other parts of houses were blown onto the ground.  At least a dozen homes were damaged.  Around 55 trees and some power lines were knocked down.  One tree knocked down was 151-years-old.

ncei:10338023.title: Near Bergen, North Dakota
ncei:10338023.narrative: The tornado was reported by many observers and by the public.  Its path was limited to the rural areas of the county.  There were no injuries and the damage was mostly to crops and trees.

ncei:10354860.title: Madisonville, Texas
ncei:10354860.narrative: Madisonville Emergency Medical Service reported four mobile homes turned over.  A 18-year-old boy witnessed the tornado.

ncei:10345851.title: Bear Creek, Pennsylvania
ncei:10345851.narrative: Two mobile homes were destroyed and several summer cottages suffered heavy damage, including being lifted from their foundation and moved several feet.  Numerous large trees were twisted and uprooted in moist soil and numerous power lines were brought down.  A dog and cat were killed.  The cat was reported blown off the porch and hurled into an adjacent yard.  There were no human fatalities or injuries.  The estimated storm damage ranged from $150,000-$200,000.
